conviction_note: Company's own monthly 6-K exhibits show self-mining output halving on a per-day basis from April to July 2026 (3.00 to 1.48 BTC/day) with a third of the installed fleet in Ethiopia going from 2.33 EH/s operating to 'paused', yet Q2 volume (244 BTC) is barely below Q1 (257) so the damage lands in the Q3 guide and the call rather than the reported quarter; the +68% 20-day run-up came from crypto policy headlines and a Hong Kong conference, not from anyone re-underwriting the mining segment, so I size the print at about one daily sigma to the downside against 183% annualised vol, net of the offsetting BTC-at-$81k treasury tailwind management will lead with.

findings.finding: Canaan's self-mining run-rate halved entering Q3 while it reported installed hashrate as flat: monthly BTC produced went 90 (April) / 90 (May) / 64 (June) / 46 (July) = 3.00 / 2.90 / 2.13 / 1.48 BTC per day, a 51% per-day decline, driven by Ethiopia (4.96 EH/s, a third of the 14.9 EH/s installed fleet) falling from 2.33 EH/s operating at 30 April to 0.36 EH/s at 30 June and then being described as 'paused' at 31 July -- yet the July release counted the entire paused 4.96 EH/s inside its headline 'operating computing power' of 14.24 EH/s, one month after the same table had shown Ethiopia at 0.36 EH/s operating.
findings.why_not_priced: Reported Q2 mining volume (90+90+64 = 244 BTC vs 257 in Q1) will look almost flat, so the deterioration is invisible in the quarter being reported and only shows up in the Q3-to-date commentary and any Q3 guide. If the market had underwritten it, the stock would not have risen 68% in the 20 sessions that straddle the 17 August release of the 46-BTC month; the two named drivers of that rally were the 20 August Trump/CLARITY Act crypto bid and the 25-27 August Bitcoin Asia conference, i.e. sector beta and a trade show. Coverage is two EPS estimates and a 'Strong Buy' consensus with a $1.72 target on a $0.36 stock, so nobody is modelling site-level uptime. The August production 6-K, on the company's own mid-month cadence (April update 14 May, May update 11 June, June update 14 July, July update 17 August), falls after the 8 September print, so the print is the first place an August number or an Ethiopia explanation can surface.
findings.independence: CryptoSlate, 2026-08-19, independently flagged that 4.96 EH/s of paused Ethiopian capacity sat inside the 14.24 EH/s operating total and that June 30 had shown Ethiopia at only 0.36 EH/s operating: https://cryptoslate.com/canaan-counted-paused-ethiopia-mining-as-nearly-35-of-its-july-operating-hashrate-total/ . Separate context, and dated 2025 not 2026, so used only as background: Ethiopian Electric Power's CEO said on 7 August 2025 there would be 'no new contracts in the field of data mining, and we are not interested in continuing with existing ones either' (https://www.cryptopolitan.com/ethiopian-electric-power-to-phase-out-mining/). The June and July hashrate tables come from two different 6-K exhibits (accessions 0001104659-26-083490 filed 2026-07-14 and 0001104659-26-097615 filed 2026-08-17) but I am treating the disclosure inconsistency and the production decline as ONE finding, not two, because they rest on the same document pair.

findings.finding: Canaan converted its automatic shelf into a $270m standard Form F-3 on 15 April 2026 specifically because it 'expects that it will cease to be a well-known seasoned issuer' on filing its FY2025 20-F, then filed Post-Effective Amendment No. 5 on 15 June 2026 as an 'exhibits-only filing to file an updated auditor consent' -- i.e. it is actively keeping a shelf equal to roughly its entire market value usable -- against cash that fell from US$80.8m at 31 December 2025 to US$43.5m at 31 March 2026, a Q1 gross LOSS of US$22.9m, US$21.1m short-term debt, and zero 424B5 takedowns anywhere in 2026 after three in 2025 (March, October, November).
findings.why_not_priced: An exhibits-only post-effective amendment to refresh an auditor consent generates no headline, no wire story and no aggregator row -- it is pure plumbing whose only purpose is to keep the shelf sellable, and it is not in the +68% run-up. If the market were pricing takedown risk you would see it in the skew, and there is no two-sided ATM option chain here at all. The specific asymmetry is timing: after ten months without using the shelf while burning ~US$37m of cash in a single quarter, the first 68% rally in a year is the first usable equity window, and a pre-open results release with an 8:00 a.m. call is where issuers of this type disclose one.
findings.independence: Points the same way but from a different document: the 4 August 2026 buyback release funds repurchases by monetising the digital asset treasury rather than from cash, and states Canaan held ~US$130m of digital assets as of 3 August -- consistent with cash being the constrained resource (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1780652/000110465926090114/tm2622168d1_ex99-1.htm, 2026-08-04). Honest counterweight from that same document: a company that announced a buyback five weeks ago is less likely to price an offering, which is why I size this small. A screener figure of 744.84m shares outstanding as of 4 September (https://stockanalysis.com/stocks/can/) sits above the 690,594,191 ADSs the company reported at 31 March 2026, but I could not confirm that from a primary filing and do not rely on it.

findings.finding: There is a mid-June 2026 open-market insider buy cluster that is essentially invisible for this name because Canaan is a 20-F/6-K filer whose officers nonetheless file Section 16 forms: CFO Cheng Jin bought 65,000 ADSs at US$0.35 on 15 June, and CEO Nangeng Zhang bought 250,000 ADSs at US$0.34 on 17 June and 250,000 at US$0.33 on 18 June, and no insider has filed any transaction since 22 June -- no sales at all into the 68% rally.
findings.why_not_priced: Insider-transaction screens and the sell-side notes on this name are built around the FPI assumption that a 20-F filer has no Section 16 reporting at all, so these Form 4s are not in any Canaan coverage I could find; had they been picked up, a CEO buying half a million ADSs three days before the low would have generated at least one wire story, and it generated none. It is also stale by twelve weeks and the purchase prices (US$0.33-0.35) sit essentially at today's US$0.36, which is exactly why I size it under one point rather than treating it as a signal about the print.
findings.independence: Separate filer, separate accession, same direction: the CEO's own Form 4 for 17-18 June at US$0.34 and US$0.33 (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1780652/000180299326000005/form4-06222026_040601.xml, filed 2026-06-22). Distinct from finding 2's documents.

findings.finding: Canaan is inside its second and final Nasdaq minimum-bid-price compliance period, expiring 11 January 2027, with the ADSs at US$0.36 -- needing roughly +178% and then ten consecutive closes at or above US$1.00 -- and the company has committed to nothing more than that it 'will evaluate all available options during the second compliance period to rectify the deficiency'; I found no depositary notice of any Canaan reverse split or ADS-ratio change, and an ADS-ratio change (currently 1 ADS = 15 Class A shares) needs no shareholder vote and can be effected in weeks.
findings.why_not_priced: The deficiency itself IS in the wire and is priced; what is not priced is that with about four months and one earnings call left, the 8 September pre-open release is the natural and cheapest venue to announce a ratio change, and the company has so far declined to name the remedy. If the market had positioned for it there would be visible put demand -- instead the chain has no two-sided ATM legs at all and put/call open interest is 0.03, i.e. essentially no downside protection outstanding. I sized this at only one point because it is a mechanical, disclosed clock rather than new information.
findings.independence: Negative check rather than confirmation: the two 2026 depositary reverse-split notices that a search for Canaan surfaced turn out to be for NIP Group Inc. (effective 6 July 2026, https://depositaryreceipts.citi.com/adr/common/file.aspx?idf=7873, notice dated 2026-06-15) and Nobia AB (effective 22 May 2026, https://depositaryreceipts.citi.com/adr/common/file.aspx?idf=7817, notice dated 2026-05-12) -- neither is Canaan, so no Canaan ratio action has been noticed to holders as of today.

searched_and_found_nothing: Any 424B5 or ATM prospectus supplement filed by Canaan in 2026 (full EDGAR submissions list checked; last was 2025-11-04), so no evidence of actual 2026 dilution, only capacity and motive
Any depositary notice of a Canaan reverse split or ADS-ratio change (the two Citi notices search returned were NIP Group Inc. and Nobia AB, not Canaan)
An August 2026 bitcoin-production 6-K -- none filed as of 2026-09-07; on the company's mid-month cadence it falls after the print

Any 2026-dated report that Ethiopian Electric Power has formally terminated or repriced Canaan's specific power contract; the EEP phase-out statements I could source are from August 2025 and the October 2025 tariff change, and I am not treating them as new
Any 10-Q, 10-K or item 2.02 8-K for Canaan -- it still files 20-F/6-K only, so there is no quarterly footnote text to diff against the prior quarter
Any disclosed completed buyback volume or dollar amount; the 4 August release and the 17 August update both stop at authorisation
Any insider Form 4 filed after 2026-06-22, in either direction, including through the 68% August rally
Any EGM/proxy notice, going-private proposal or 13D-style activist filing (only passive 13G/13G-A filings on 2026-06-05, 08-11 and 08-13)
Customer-side surfaces that exist for consumer names but not for a rig vendor: no app-store reviews, no support forum with a live complaint thread, no status page
Any government contract award, port or shipping datapoint tying to A15/A16 rig shipment volumes
baseline_tension: The baseline offers no skew and no implied move to cut against, so the only thing to beat is the +68% 20-day run-up -- and my main finding cuts directly against it, because that rally is attributable to crypto-policy headlines and a Hong Kong trade show over exactly the window in which the company's own filings showed its per-day bitcoin production falling 51% and a third of its fleet going dark.
